One of India's great Sun temples, dedicated to Surya, on the bank of the Pushpavati river. Built in 1026-27 CE by Bhima I of the Chaulukya (Solanki) dynasty in Maru-Gurjara style. The complex has three axial parts aligned on the Tropic of Cancer: the Surya Kund step tank with 108 shrines, the 52-pillared Sabha Mandapa, and the Guda Mandapa sanctum. The Skanda and Brahma Puranas link Modhera to the Ramayana-era Dharmaranya forest. The temple was desecrated - popular accounts name Mahmud Ghazni and later Allauddin Khilji (early 1300s); the main Surya idol was lost and no worship has been offered since. An ASI-protected monument of national importance; the annual Modhera Dance Festival (Uttarardh Mahotsav) is held here each January.

name: Modhera Sun Temple
town_description: Modhera is a village in Mehsana district of north Gujarat on the Pushpavati river. Said to have been the original settlement of the Modha Brahmins, it is steeped in legend - the Skanda Purana places Rama's yajna here in the forest of Dharmaranya. The village is dominated by the 11th-century Sun Temple complex, now an ASI monument and the venue of the annual Modhera Dance Festival.
